text:
maria: Quick follow-up on the LingerPool / residency API RFC. Thinking of exposing a per-allocation 'linger' window to reduce churn when pages bounce between GPU and host. TL;DR: small per-allocation hint that keeps pages around short-term instead of immediate eviction. Thoughts?
ajay: Nice. How are we measuring the tradeoff? memory cost vs token throughput?
maria: Early sim with chat workload shows +8-12% token throughput (lower stall on assistant turns) for linger_ms=200-400ms, but host memory pressure up a few percent.
tessa: We need telemetry before we can tune defaults: linger_active, linger_evicted, linger_hits, linger_alloc_ms. Also watch tail latencies.
rick: Fragmentation worry: if many allocations linger on host, we might create lots of tiny free holes on GPU. Can linger be scoped to coarse-grained pages or superblocks?
hana: API shape suggestion (minimal): ResidencyHint { linger_ms: u32, prefer_gpu: bool }. Implementation: per-NUMA linger pools that hold host-backed pages for X ms before returning to eviction.
maria: Agree minimal v1. Keep interface small so customers can opt-in. Implementation details: allocator will tag allocations with hint and move to linger pool on free instead of immediate reclaim. Linger pool eviction still subject to pressure.
ajay: What's failure-mode? If linger pool blocks allocation on heavy pressure, we must bypass and evict immediately. Also prefetch vs keep-on-host decision - how do we encode?
hana: Keep prefetch separate. ResidencyHint shouldn't change prefetch behavior initially. If prefer_gpu=true, allocator will try to keep replica on GPU when possible, else linger on host shorter.
tessa: Can we surface linger_score in traces? e.g., "allocation->linger_ms" so we can correlate with p99.
maria: Yes. Plan: add structured trace events for linger-enter / linger-evict with tags: alloc_id, model, task_type, linger_ms.

```
# pseudo API
runtime.set_residency_hint(model="gpt-4o-x", hint={
  "linger_ms": 300,
  "prefer_gpu": true
})
```

devploy-bot: deploy queued for branch: feature/linger-proto (staging) :rocket:

rick: runtime-level policy question: should linger be applied by default to ephemeral KV caches? that might save recompute.
ajay: For KV caches it's probably good. But we need unit tests: simulate workloads with various reuse distances.
tessa: Also add gauge metrics: linger_pool_size_{node}, linger_pool_pressure_{node}. Alerts for linger_pool_size > threshold sustained.
maria: Rollout plan: 1) prototype in staging with opt-in param per-model, 2) run perf suite (ajay), 3) collect telemetry for 2 weeks, 4) iterate.
hana: Implementation note: make linger pool per-allocator-instance so different backends (dedicated vs private) can tune separately.
ajay: Who owns perf runs? I can do a baseline vs linger=off/200/400/800 for 48h.
maria: Thanks. I'll open the RFC follow-up PR with design + pseudo API + telemetry checklist. Assign: @ajay perf, @tessa telemetry, @hana impl prototype. Sync Thursday 10am.

maria: One more thing — compatibility: when rolling out, ensure older runners without linger simply ignore the hint (backwards compatible).
tessa: ACK. We'll add a versioned hint header so older servers drop it.

maria: Cool. If no blockers, I'll spawn the PR and draft the perf matrix. :+1:
